clues.title: Pole: octagonal concrete with engravings
text: Most utility poles in Mexico are made of concrete and have an **octagonal shape**. There will often be engravings on the side.
NOTE: Octagonal poles are also common in Colombia.
clues.summary: Most poles are concrete and eight-sided, often with engravings on the side. Colombia has octagonal poles too.

clues.title: Plate: short, many designs
text: Mexico uses short licence plates with a large variety of designs. Front plates are required.
NOTE: For an overview of the most common regional designs, see step 2.
clues.summary: Short plates in a great variety of designs, and front plates are required. Each state has its own designs (see the plate infographic).

clues.title: Road lines: white edges
text: The most typical Mexican road lines are white solid outer lines with a **single unbroken yellow middle line**.
NOTE: [Single](https://goo.gl/maps/Dbjb5sJ1xcrQBTof7) broken yellow middle lines and [double](https://goo.gl/maps/L9YSqFc6h79idwkm8) yellow middle lines are also common.
clues.summary: The typical lines are solid white edges with a single unbroken yellow centre line. A single broken yellow centre or double yellow centre are also common.

clues.title: Bollard: small white cylinder, black base
text: These small, **cylindrical** white bollards with a **black base** are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector can sometimes be seen, as well as a flat version.
clues.summary: A small, cylindrical white bollard with a black base, unique here. A yellow reflector is sometimes seen, and there is also a flat version.

clues.title: Road shields: curvy national
text: Mexico has two general road shields; one for national highways with “MEXICO” written at the top and a slightly curvy design, and one for state roads which have straight borders, and typically has the state initials written at the top.
clues.summary: Two shields: national highways have a slightly curvy shape with the country name on top, and state roads have straight borders, usually with state initials on top.

clues.title: Sign: large all-caps white direction font
text: Mexican directional signs have a distinctly large, **all-caps** white font.
clues.summary: Direction signs use a distinctly large, all-caps white font.

clues.title: Road: white km markers, black text and outline
text: Mexican **kilometre markers** are white, with black font and outline.
clues.summary: Kilometre markers are white with black lettering and outline, set at hip height with "km" and the number stacked vertically.

clues.title: Plants: many kinds of cacti everywhere
text: **Cacti**, of many different species, are extremely common in Mexico.
clues.summary: Cacti of many species are extremely common.

clues.title: Sign: stop sign reading ALTO
text: Mexico uses the word “ALTO” on stop signs.
NOTE: All of South America, as well as Puerto Rico, use the word “PARE”. Panama, Costa Rica, and Guatemala also use “ALTO”.
clues.summary: Stop signs say "ALTO". Panama, Costa Rica and Guatemala use it too. All of South America and Puerto Rico say "PARE".

clues.title: Sign: very thick arrows
text: Arrows on signs are noticeably **very thick**.
clues.summary: Arrows on signs are noticeably thick, compared with other countries in the Americas.

clues.title: Road: yellow accents on kerbs and bridge
text: **Yellow **accents on kerbs and bridge barriers are quite common.
clues.summary: Yellow marking on kerbs and bridge barriers is quite common.

clues.title: Rooftops: wide cylindrical black or white
text: You will commonly see wide cylindrical, **black or white water tanks** on rooftops.
clues.summary: Wide cylindrical black or white water tanks are often on rooftops.

clues.title: Shops: OXXO and Pemex
text: **OXXO** and **Pemex** are two of the most popular gas station brands in Mexico.

NOTE: While less common, OXXO can still be found in [other countries](https://www.google.com/maps/@-33.4481518,-70.5764202,3a,15y,199.57h,89.44t,1.18r/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1sJaAVdAE4oby9-yp1rsx3PQ!2e0!5s20230501T000000!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: OXXO and Pemex are two of the most popular fuel and convenience brands. OXXO can still be found, less often, in other countries.

clues.title: Place names: lots of x, tl, -ec, -tlan
text: Many place names in Mexico are of [Nahuatl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahuatl) origin, featuring a lot of ‘x’ and ‘tl’ as well as ‘-ec’ and ‘-tlan’ suffixes.
clues.summary: Many place names come from Nahuatl, with plenty of x and tl and endings like -ec and -tlan.

clues.title: Houses: round electricity meters
text: Mexico uses **circular** electricity counters.
NOTE: Circular electricity counters are not unique to Mexico and can also be found in the US, Guatemala, Dominican Republic and the Philippines.
clues.summary: Round electricity meters are used. The US, Guatemala, Dominican Republic and the Philippines have them too.

clues.title: Cars: lots of US brands and pickups
text: United States car brands are popular in Mexico. In particular, you will see a lot of **pickup trucks**.
clues.summary: US car brands are popular, with a lot of pickup trucks.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 2 coverage exists
text: Mexico is one of very few Latin American countries that has **Generation 2 coverage**.
NOTE: Brazil has some Generation 2, but it is considerably more rare, as most of it is overwritten.
clues.summary: One of very few Latin American countries with the older Gen 2 camera (lower quality). Brazil has some but much rarer, since most was overwritten.

clues.title: Google car: white Gen 3
text: The Generation 3 coverage in Mexico mainly feature two cars:
- A white car with a **stubby antenna**. There is a diagonal coil wrapped around the antenna.
- A white car with a more **visible **back and a long red **brake light** instead of an antenna.
It is possible to find a white car without a stubby antenna, but with a tiny [sliver](https://goo.gl/maps/qxynyEHgmp85RBmu5) visible where the antenna should be.
clues.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage mainly shows two cars: a white car with a stubby antenna wrapped in a diagonal coil, and a white car with a more visible back and a long red brake light instead of an antenna. You may also see a white car with only a tiny sliver where the antenna should be.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4, visible front, blue
text: The Generation 4 cars in Mexico commonly have a visible front and can feature various different colour patterns. The three most common ones are:
- Blue
- White with a blue stripe
- Black
clues.summary: Newer Gen 4 cars often show the front and come in several colour schemes. The three most common are blue, white with a blue stripe, and black.

clues.title: Phone numbers: first digit shows the region
text: The first digit of Mexican **area codes** are regional and can be seen on this map.
clues.summary: The first digit of area codes is regional. See the map.

clues.title: Postal codes: on street signs
text: Similarly, Mexican **postal codes** can be seen on this map. They will commonly appear at the [bottom of street signs](https://goo.gl/maps/8bgZx7q8pjzzFSYi6), and are ordered alphabetically based on state names.
clues.summary: Postal codes usually appear at the bottom of street signs and are ordered alphabetically by state name. See the map.

clues.title: Plate: every state has its own design
text: Every state in Mexico has one or several unique licence plate designs. In this infographic you can find the most common and helpful ones.
clues.summary: Each state has one or more unique plate designs. The infographic shows the most common and helpful ones.

clues.title: Plants: prickly pear with flat oval pads
text: **Prickly pear cacti** are distinct with their **flat oval-shaped pads**. They are noticeably more common centrally and are rarely seen in southern and coastal states.
clues.summary: Prickly pear cacti have flat, oval pads. They are noticeably more common in the centre and rarely seen in the south and coastal states.

clues.title: Plants: pulque agave
text: Agave salmiana, also known as **pulque agaves**, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a **crown-like** appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.
clues.summary: Agave salmiana has wide, smooth, curling leaves in a crown shape. Common in the central valley and further north around San Luis Potosí.

clues.title: Crops: vast fields of blue agave
text: Vast fields of **blue agave** (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.
clues.summary: Vast fields of blue agave (for tequila), mostly in Jalisco and Nayarit.

clues.title: Plants: tree yucca, oblong rosettes on a trunk
text: Yucca filifera, also known as **tree yucca**, as well as yucca decipiens are most commonly seen in San Luis Potosi and Zacatecas as well as some of the bordering northern states. They can be recognised by their oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves branching from a single trunk, similar to a tree.
clues.summary: Yucca filifera (tree yucca) and Y. decipiens, mostly in San Luis Potosí and Zacatecas and some bordering northern states. Oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves on a single tree-like trunk.

clues.title: Plants: giant cardon, sprawling arms, ribbed
text: The **Mexican Giant Cardon** is an extremely common cacti in the Baja California peninsula. It can be identified through its large sprawling arms stemming from a singular trunk and ribbed exterior.
clues.summary: The giant cardon is extremely common in Baja California: large sprawling arms from one ribbed trunk.

clues.title: Plants: saguaro, short curving arms
text: The **Saguaro** **Cacti** can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.
clues.summary: Saguaro cacti grow in the western half of Sonora, with short curving arms from a main trunk.

clues.title: Plants: organ pipe
text: **Organ Pipe Cacti** have long thin stems that often come out from a stem that is around ground level. They are most commonly found in Sonora and occasionally in Baja California Sur.
clues.summary: Organ pipe cacti have long thin stems sprouting near ground level. Most common in Sonora and occasionally Baja California Sur.

clues.title: Plants: blue myrtle cactus, short upturned arms
text: The **Blue Myrtle Cacti** have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.
clues.summary: Short arms that curve uniformly upward. Abundant in San Luis Potosí and also common in Querétaro and Hidalgo.

clues.title: Crops: sugar cane, most in the east
text: **Sugar cane** can be found all over the country, but by far most common in Veracruz.
clues.summary: Sugar cane grows nationwide but by far the most in Veracruz.

clues.title: Plants: coconut palms in coastal groups
text: **Coconut palms **can be found all across the coast, but are often found in large groups in Guerrero and Colima.
clues.summary: Coconut palms grow all along the coast, often in big groups in Guerrero and Colima.

clues.title: Plants: sabal palm, lollipop sun-shaped crown
text: **Sabal palms **are most commonly observed in the east coast of Mexico, the Yucatan peninsula, as well as the state of Nayarit. They feature a spiky, sun-shaped crown, giving the tree a** lollipop-like **appearance.
clues.summary: Sabal palms are mostly on the east coast, the Yucatán peninsula and Nayarit, with a spiky, sun-shaped crown like a lollipop.

clues.title: Plants: huge palm with upright umbrella-like
text: The **Attalea rostrata **is a huge palm recognizable from its upright leaves, almost resembling an umbrella. It is mostly exclusive to Veracruz and Tabasco, and can be rarely found in Chiapas.
clues.summary: Attalea rostrata has upright leaves resembling an umbrella. Mostly in Veracruz and Tabasco, rarely in Chiapas.

clues.title: Crops: oil palm plantations
text: **Oil palm plantations **are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.
clues.summary: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the edges in Veracruz, Tabasco and Campeche.

clues.title: Plants: boojum tree, alien tentacle look
text: **Boojum trees** can be recognized by their alien, **tentacle**-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.
clues.summary: Boojum trees look alien and tentacle-like. Almost only in the southern half of Baja California.

clues.title: Plants: small bright silver-grey shrubs
text: **Brittlebush** are small shrubs with bright **silver-grey** leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.
clues.summary: Brittlebush is a small shrub with bright silver-grey leaves, most common in Sonora especially around Hermosillo.

clues.title: Plants: thin white-barked trees
text: These **thin, white-barked **trees can be found in the Yucatan peninsula, but are most prevalent in Quintana Roo.
clues.summary: Thin trees with white bark on the Yucatán peninsula, most common in Quintana Roo.

clues.title: Plants: gold grass tufts in a line by the road
text: These **gold tufts** of grass in a line right next to the road are most commonly found in Coahuila.
clues.summary: Gold tufts of grass in a line right by the road are most common in Coahuila.

clues.title: Plants: teardrop-shaped grass clumps
text: These **clumps **of grass in almost a teardrop shape are common in the region around Tlaxcala.
clues.summary: Clumps of grass shaped almost like teardrops, common around Tlaxcala.

clues.title: Farmland: red agricultural fields
text: **Red agricultural fields** are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.
clues.summary: Red farm fields are common in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

clues.title: Landscape: tall mountain ranges surrounding a
text: The Monterrey metropolitan area features tall stunning **mountain ranges** that surround the city.
clues.summary: The Monterrey area is ringed by tall, striking mountain ranges.

clues.title: Landscape: rocky pine mountains
text: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with **pine forests**. In general, these pines are shorter and more **stunted **in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.
clues.summary: West Chihuahua and Durango can be rocky and mountainous with pine forests. The pines are shorter and more stunted than in the centre or south.

clues.title: Farmland: extremely dark fields
text: **Extremely dark fields** are common in Guanajuato.
clues.summary: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

clues.title: Landscape: reddish-brown hills with big
text: These **reddish brown-tinged** hills, often accompanied by **large boulders**, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.
clues.summary: Reddish-brown hills often with large boulders are common in the northern half of Baja California.

clues.title: Soil: blindingly white
text: Almost **blindingly white** soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.
NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.
clues.summary: Almost blindingly white soil on the Yucatán peninsula, most common in Quintana Roo. Only consistent in Gen 3.

clues.title: Farmland: red fields among dense tropical
text: These **red agricultural fields** surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.
clues.summary: Red farm fields surrounded by dense tropical forest, most common in northern Campeche.

clues.title: Houses: red brick, mostly west of the capital
text: **Red brick** buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.
clues.summary: Red brick buildings are concentrated in the states west of Mexico City: Jalisco, Michoacán, Guanajuato and Aguascalientes.

clues.title: Houses: white concrete blocks around the
text: **White concrete block **buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east. They can however still be found all over the country.
clues.summary: White concrete block buildings are concentrated in the states around Mexico City, more to the east, but found everywhere.

clues.title: Houses: mud brick, whole houses
text: **Mud brick** buildings are most abundant in Durango, especially full houses constructed with mud brick. However, they can essentially be found in almost all of the dry desert states.
clues.summary: Mud brick buildings are most common in Durango, especially entire houses, and appear in almost all the dry desert states.

clues.title: Houses: US bungalow style, pastel, gated
text: Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows. Many houses are coloured with **light **or **pastel **colours, **gated **and commonly have front yards. **Orange tiles** inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.
clues.summary: In the north, houses borrow from American bungalows: light or pastel colours, gates and front yards, plus orange Spanish-colonial style tiles.

clues.title: Roofs: thatched
text: **Thatched roofs** are most common in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi. They can also be found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.
clues.summary: Thatched roofs are most common on the Yucatán peninsula and in eastern San Luis Potosí, and found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

clues.title: Walls: light-coloured rock
text: These walls made of **light coloured rock** are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.
clues.summary: Walls of light-coloured rock on the Yucatán peninsula, most common in Yucatán state. They look darker out of the sun.

clues.title: Sign back: thick cross
text: A thick **cross** can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.
clues.summary: A thick cross on the back of road signs in Chihuahua.

clues.title: Bollard: red band near the top
text: Bollards with a **red band** near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from [one exception](https://www.google.com/maps/@16.416407,-94.109672,3a,15y,95.28h,64.73t,0.03r/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1s_lRtg1MKWPSNX_dJch3kig!2e0!5s20220501T000000!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu) being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.
clues.summary: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, with one exception: Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

clues.title: Bollard: crown and name written on it
text: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a **crown** and the text ‘**Jalisco**’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

images.caption: White post with a crest and name printed on it, circled in red

clues.summary: Jalisco bollards sometimes have a crown and the state name on them. Hard to read unless close, but no other bollard here has writing.

clues.title: Pole: white acorn-shaped insulators
text: **White insulators** that are shaped like acorns can be found along the coastal states of Mexico, but are by far most common in Michoacan, Colima, and Veracruz.

images.caption: A pole top with a crossbar and three white insulators

clues.summary: White acorn-shaped insulators appear in coastal states, most of all in Michoacán, Colima and Veracruz.

clues.title: Pole: asymmetric crossbar
text: Poles with an **asymmetric crossbar **and **double-stacked **insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.
clues.summary: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are only in Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo and Morelos.

clues.title: Pole: wooden with a lowered crossbar
text: **Wooden **poles with a **lowered crossbar** are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.
clues.summary: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly in Sinaloa and Sonora.

clues.title: Pole: concrete
text: These concrete poles with insulators **suspended below **the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.
clues.summary: Concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatán peninsula.

clues.title: Pole: wooden version with hanging insulators
text: The **wooden **variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.
clues.summary: The wooden version of the hanging pole is on the Baja California peninsula.

clues.title: Pole: lowered crossbar with a single brace
text: Poles with a lowered crossbar and a **single support beam** that extend from one end of the crossbar to the pole itself can be found in Durango.
clues.summary: Poles with a lowered crossbar and one support beam running from one end of the crossbar to the pole, found in Durango.

clues.title: Pole: mesh body
text: Poles with a** mesh body** are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.
clues.summary: Poles with a mesh body are most common in San Luis Potosí, Guanajuato and Querétaro.

clues.title: Road lines: white centre line
text: **White **middle roadlines are most commonly found in Tabasco.
clues.summary: White centre lines are most common in Tabasco.

clues.title: Fences: living trees with red bark
text: These fences made out of trees with **red-coloured bark **are commonly found in Veracruz.
NOTE: These tree fences can still be found in other coastal states and are best utilised when combined with other clues.
clues.summary: Fences made of trees with red-coloured bark are common in Veracruz. They also occur in other coastal states, so combine with other clues.

clues.title: Road lines: black tar on both sides of yellow
text: **Black tar** on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.
NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.
clues.summary: Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line appears in Sinaloa, Durango and Guerrero. Most reliable when the tar is not faded.

clues.title: Road: grainy blue-grey pavement
text: **Grainy **pavement with a** blue-ish grey tinge** is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.
NOTE: In Tamaulipas, larger roads very commonly feature [dashed outer lines](https://goo.gl/maps/J82S2uF1oZ7qGhEG6).
clues.summary: Grainy pavement with a bluish-grey tinge is common in Tamaulipas and Nuevo León. In Tamaulipas larger roads often have dashed outer lines.

clues.title: Ground: messy irregular cobblestone
text: This style of **cobblestone pavement**, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.
clues.summary: Unorganised cobblestone with irregular tiles is in most central states, but most common in Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Querétaro.

clues.title: Ground: hexagonal tile paving
text: This pavement consisting of **hexagonal tiles** is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
clues.summary: Pavement of hexagonal tiles is in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

clues.title: Ground: three lines of cobblestone pattern
text: This exact pavement design with **three lines** of cobblestone patterning is mainly found in Oaxaca.
clues.summary: This exact paving with three lines of cobblestone patterning is mainly in Oaxaca.

clues.title: Taxi: white lower half, pink upper half
text: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half with a **pink upper half**.
clues.summary: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half and a pink upper half.

clues.title: Landscape: flat farmland, ridge west
text: The area around **Mexicali** features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. [Washingtonia](https://goo.gl/maps/Z9JhouH2WnYeJW1z8)[ palms](https://goo.gl/maps/Z9JhouH2WnYeJW1z8) are very common and these [poles](https://goo.gl/maps/JG3LABTi1T4aSrzc9) made out of brown wood can be found.

images.caption: Flat farmland beside a dirt road

clues.summary: Around Mexicali: flat farmland with a ridge to the west, very common Washingtonia palms and brown wooden poles.

clues.title: Plants: citrus plantations on hilltops
text: The area around Poza Rica in Veracruz features a lot of **citrus tree plantations**. It is common to see large amounts of these trees grown right on top of the hills.
clues.summary: Around Poza Rica in Veracruz many citrus plantations, often grown right on top of hills.

clues.title: Landscape: pinkish-tan soil and canals around
text: The area around Ciudad Obregon is distinct due to the **pinkish-tan soil **and **canals **found around the city’s agricultural areas.
clues.summary: Around Ciudad Obregón: pinkish-tan soil and canals around the farmland.

clues.title: Landscape: twin volcanoes
text: The **twin volcanoes** of Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl are found on the border between the State of Mexico and Puebla. Keep in mind that they are [usually much less visible](https://goo.gl/maps/3zngjfu2ucdDwvcV6) than depicted in the image, which is just for reference.
clues.summary: The twin volcanoes Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl sit on the border of the State of Mexico and Puebla. They are usually much less visible than in the reference photo.

clues.title: Landscape: distinct extinct volcano
text: **Cerro del Bernal **is a distinct extinct volcano that is found in southern Tamaulipas. It can be found heading directly northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.
clues.summary: Cerro del Bernal, a distinct extinct volcano in southern Tamaulipas, northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.

clues.title: Landscape: extremely long flat ridge
text: This extremely **long **and **flat ridge** is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.
clues.summary: An extremely long, flat ridge in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosí.

clues.title: Landscape: tall flat ridge with prominent
text: This tall, flat ridge, with very **prominent ridgelines**, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border.
NOTE: The only road the mountain range can be observed from is the Federal Highway 53 that leads to Boquillas del Carmen.
clues.summary: A tall flat ridge in the Maderas del Carmen reserve in northern Coahuila near the US border, seen only from Federal Highway 53.

differs.how: Near the US border but only seen from one highway

clues.title: Landscape: orange-soil dirt roads, low shrubs
text: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez features a lot of dirt roads with a distinct shade of **orange soil **and **low shrubs**.
clues.summary: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez have lots of dirt roads with a distinct orange soil and low shrubs.

clues.title: Landscape: rolling hills alternating orange
text: The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct **orange **and **beige**-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more [prominent](https://goo.gl/maps/HzfgXbCXgYegsKodA) in some locations.
clues.summary: Around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south in Oaxaca, rolling hills with distinct orange and beige soil that changes with each hill.

clues.title: Landscape: jagged cliffs, pinkish soil
text: The town of Guaymas has a lot of **jagged **cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.
clues.summary: Around Guaymas: jagged cliffs and mountains, distinctly pinkish soil, and organ pipe cacti on the hills and beside the road.

clues.title: Landmark: pink lakes
text: The town of Las Coloradas is famously known for the **pink lakes** around the area.
clues.summary: Las Coloradas is famous for the pink lakes around the area.

clues.title: Road: divided highway, yucca on both sides
text: The 54 is a divided highway that runs through northeastern Zacatecas which features **yucca trees** spammed on both sides of the road. Additionally, the streetview car is often exposed and appears almost [white](https://goo.gl/maps/BfA6FLRVcL371P9z9) due to the sunlight.
clues.summary: The 54 is a divided highway through northeastern Zacatecas with yucca trees on both sides. The Street View car is often exposed and looks almost white in the sun.

clues.title: Road: lush cliffs, tunnels
text: The 40D that crosses the Sinaloa-Durango state line is recognizable by the stunning lush **cliffs **and mountains along the road. The highway commonly passes through tunnels and the road itself features **double yellow** middle roadlines.
clues.summary: The 40D across the Sinaloa-Durango line has lush cliffs and mountains, frequent tunnels and double yellow centre lines.

clues.title: Road divider: yellow top and bottom edge
text: This road divider with a **yellow** **top **and **bottom **edge is found all along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.

images.caption: Crash-barrier divider with yellow top and bottom edges, seen beside the road

clues.summary: A road divider with yellow top and bottom edges runs along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.

clues.title: Landmark: rows of wind turbines
text: The Eurus Wind Farm is located in southeast Oaxaca and is the largest wind farm in Mexico. Rows of **wind turbines** can be found along the 190 around Juchitán de Zaragoza.

clues.title: Plants: palm with large stiff pointy leaves
text: This palm seems to be prominent in coastal Texas, the east and the south coast of Mexico, Yucatán peninsula, and Guatemala. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.
Sabal Mexicana has **large, stiff, pointy leaves** and densely packed.
Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

images.caption: Fan palm with red lines marking its large stiff leaves, labelled with the species name
Three fan palms labelled with their species names

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Sabal mexicana has large, stiff, pointy, densely packed leaves. Found in the east and south coast, the Yucatán and Guatemala. Sabal yapa droops and looks shredded; sabal rosei has visible gaps and brighter green leaves.

clues.title: Plants: palm with visible leaf gaps
text: Sabal Rosei is native to the Pacific coast of Mexico, from Sinaloa to Jalisco but mostly concentrated in the state of Nayarit. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.
Sabal Rosei tends to have **visible gaps between the leaves**, and they are a **brighter green color**.
Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.

images.caption: Fan palm with red ovals marking the gaps between its leaves, labelled S. rosei

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Sabal rosei grows on the Pacific coast, from Sinaloa to Jalisco, mostly in Nayarit. Its leaves have visible gaps and a brighter green than the other sabal palms.

clues.title: Plants: palm with drooping, shredded-tip leaves
text: This palm grows pretty much exclusively in the Yucatán peninsula. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.
Sabal Yapa has **droopy, hanging leaves** that almost look **shredded** at the tips.
Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

images.caption: Palm with red lines tracing its drooping, shredded leaf tips, labelled S. yapa

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Sabal yapa grows almost only on the Yucatán peninsula. Its leaves droop and look shredded at the tips.

clues.title: Plants: pitaya with branches curling from a
text: In Pitaya the branches less organically sprout from the ground in the weed-like manner of the Organ Pipe, and instead curl smoothly outwards from a **central stem**.
It is mostly found in Jalisco, south of Guadalajara. Less commonly, it's seen in Guanajuato. It can be seen in Queretaro too, but surprisingly rarely.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Branches curl smoothly outwards from a central stem, unlike the weed-like organ pipe. Mostly south of Guadalajara in Jalisco, less often Guanajuato, and surprisingly rarely Querétaro.

clues.title: Plants: tall cactus with thin twirling branches
text: A rare and tall cactus, the thin and twirling branches of S. fricii are unique to Michoacan, especially on the 37D, where it is abundantly spammed.

clues.summary: A rare tall cactus (Stenocereus fricii) with thin, twirling branches, unique to Michoacán and very abundant on the 37D.

clues.title: Plants: tree cholla, skeletal discoloured arms
text: The tree cholla is a cactus, and its skeletal, discoloured arms spurting in every direction make it recognisable.
Mostly found in San Luis Potosi, Queretaro and Hidalgo, often in Coahuila and Durango and rarely in Zacatecas.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Tree cholla has skeletal, discoloured arms sprouting in every direction. Mostly in San Luis Potosí, Querétaro and Hidalgo, often in Coahuila and Durango, rarely in Zacatecas.

clues.title: Plants: slick lime-green agave
text: Agave lechuguilla is a very frequent sighting in the hills of Durango and Coahuila, particularly around the cities of Saltillo and west of Torreon. More rarely it can be found in San Luis Potosi and Hidalgo. It is distinguished by its slick, lime-green leaves that almost look as if they are combed to one side.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Agave lechuguilla is common in the hills of Durango and Coahuila, especially around Saltillo and west of Torreón, more rarely San Luis Potosí and Hidalgo. Slick lime-green leaves that look combed to one side.

clues.title: Plants: small bluish agave, hard to spot
text: The rough century plant looks similar to the pulque agave but its leaves are blueish and it is much smaller. It is distributed nearly identically to A. lechuguilla (Durango and Coahuila, especially around Saltillo and West of Torreon, rarely SLP and Hidalgo), and is often difficult to spot from the road, only barely visible in the distance in batches.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The rough century plant looks like the pulque agave but is bluish and much smaller. It has nearly the same range as lechuguilla (Durango, Coahuila around Saltillo and west of Torreón), and is often only barely visible in batches in the distance.

clues.title: Plants: agave with thin spiky cylindrical leaf
text: A. karwinskii is exclusively seen in the central desert region of Oaxaca, mostly near the town Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz, even though technically its native distribution extends elsewhere in the state and barely into Puebla. Its spiky thin leaves, protruding from the centre in a cylindrical formation, make it quite distinct from other common agaves.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A. karwinskii is only in the central desert of Oaxaca, mostly near Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz. Spiky thin leaves in a cylindrical shape set it apart from other agaves.

clues.title: Plants: cup-shaped agave on walls
text: Agave cupreata is a very rarely observed agave that is localised to central Guerrero. Its name is apt - it has a much more pronounced, cup-like appearance than other agaves, with the leaves lurching inwards. It is often found growing on walls in groups as depicted.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Agave cupreata is very rare and found in central Guerrero. It has a pronounced cup shape with leaves curving inwards, often growing in groups on walls.

clues.title: Farmland: prickly pear plantations on plains
text: In the northeast most area of State of Mexico, around the town **Nopaltepec**, they often farm Opuntia in vast plains. Farms of prickly pear are otherwise most commonly found in **north east Morelos**, where they foreground striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. These farms can be found randomly elsewhere in the country, but much less commonly; if there is a third most common location for them it would be **Guanajuato**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: In the far northeast of the State of Mexico around Nopaltepec, prickly pear is farmed in vast plains. Otherwise most common in northeast Morelos in front of eroded dry hills, and possibly Guanajuato third.

clues.title: Plants: only prickly pear, no other succulents
text: Prickly pear cacti with a total absence of other cacti, yucca, agaves or in general succulent plants except for the prickly pear is generally a good signal for the centre-west (Jalisco, Guanajuato, Michoacan).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Prickly pear with no other cacti, yucca, agaves or succulents is generally a good sign of the centre-west: Jalisco, Guanajuato or Michoacán.

clues.title: Plants: dense branches
text: The Indian Comb (Pachycereus pecten-aboriginum), is a common cactus that always implies Sinaloa, or south Sonora near Sinaloa, although technically its habitat extends elsewhere. Its densely packed branches emerge from a single stem, but most recognisable is its inflorescence - the brightly coloured flowers which usually adorn the tip of its arms.

clues.summary: The Indian comb (Pachycereus pecten-aboriginum) always suggests Sinaloa or south Sonora near Sinaloa. Dense branches from one stem and bright flowers at the tips of the arms.
